articles.title: Netherlands Seizes 800 Servers, Arrests 2 for Aiding Cyberattacks
articles.summary: Meta's AI support bot just became the perfect social engineering target, letting hackers seize high-profile Instagram accounts including Obama's White House account. When your AI is dumber than a phishing email, maybe it's time to rethink automation.

articles.title: VICTORY: Meta Strips Facial Recognition Code From Smart Glasses App After Public Outcry
articles.summary: CISA contractor casually dumps AWS GovCloud keys on GitHub like it's their personal notepad. The agency tasked with protecting critical infrastructure just leaked their own crown jewels—chef's kiss of irony.

articles.title: Iran Signed a Ceasefire — Its Hackers Didn't
articles.summary: Check Point VPN zero-day gets exploited by Qilin ransomware for over a month before anyone notices. Nothing says 'enterprise security' like giving attackers a month-long head start.

articles.title: Chrome's zero-day Whac-A-Mole continues with fifth exploited bug of the year
articles.summary: Signal tells UK government their plan to scan devices for nude images 'endangers us all.' Because nothing could possibly go wrong with mandatory government backdoors masquerading as child protection.

articles.title: France probes compromise of gov messaging platform after account hijack
articles.summary: Chrome's fifth exploited zero-day of the year proves Google's Whac-A-Mole security strategy. At least they paid the researcher $55K—more than most people make finding Chrome bugs the hard way.

articles.title: A Qilin ransomware affiliate exploited a Check Point VPN zero-day for a month before a patch existed
articles.summary: University of Toronto researchers build self-replicating AI worm that operates entirely on local models. Because apparently regular malware wasn't scary enough—now it can think for itself.

articles.title: Ransomware crims got a month-long head start on Check Point VPN 0-day that now has a fix
articles.summary: WhatsApp catches NSO Group violating court orders like the digital arms dealers they are. Turns out telling spyware companies to 'please stop' works about as well as you'd expect.

articles.title: Gogs patches critical zero-day enabling remote code execution
articles.summary: Former IBM exec blows whistle on company covering up years of Chinese state hacking. Big Blue apparently thought 'security through obscurity' meant hiding breaches from their own customers.

articles.title: ⚡ Weekly Recap: Instagram Account Hacks, Android Zero-Day, GitHub Worm and More
articles.summary: Gogs patches critical zero-day enabling remote code execution on any public instance. Git repositories: where your code goes to die, apparently.

articles.title: WinRAR Flaw Exploited by Russia-Aligned Groups to Deploy Stealers in Ukraine
articles.summary: Microsoft takes GitHub repos offline after Miasma worm infects 73 open-source projects. When even Microsoft's own code gets pwned, you know supply chain attacks have reached peak lulz.
